method: Same cloud instance: 60s extras closed, 60s after two extra-market games become healthy, 60s closed again. Main SSE and 10s metric sampling are identical. Cloud-clock calibration precedes each measured phase; source health and SSE silence are checked each second.
limitations: Sequential windows cannot remove upstream/network variation or prove causal zero overhead.
FanDuel completed polling cycles per second measure collector throughput, not bookmaker-change latency, push latency or browser paint.
SSE receive gaps include freshness and heartbeats and are transport continuity measurements only.
This run tests availability and error counters; independent quote-by-quote verification is a separate test.
No finite sample proves permanent zero overhead or 100% accuracy.
History persistence remains enabled in every phase; checkpoint timing is recorded but not controlled.

notes: Browser samples are client-reported estimates after two animation frames, corrected using /api/time. Inspect clock uncertainty.
DraftKings createdTime is the provider feed timestamp, not a verified trading-engine change timestamp. Cross-host clock skew can affect it.
FanDuel push updatedAt has whole-second precision. Its age is an upper-bound estimate with up to about 999ms quantization plus unmeasured provider clock skew; HTTP prices have no change timestamp.

FanDuel uses immediate push alongside 250ms HTTP checks, continuing HTTP if push is unavailable. Nominal polling wait averages half the interval only for uniformly timed changes without delays; this is not a measured end-to-end guarantee or a maximum price age.
Live rows with n=0 mean not measured; pregame results must not be presented as live results.
